events.assessment: The flagged online transaction 3612011 is low-value and aligns with the card's historical baseline of online activity, but it was conducted via an anonymous proxy. Additionally, the 72-hour window reveals a highly suspicious rapid-fire sequence of three nearly identical in-person transactions (3587491, 3587492, and 3587495) within a 44-second span, suggesting potential card testing or terminal abuse.
key_points: Flagged transaction 3612011 ($34.22) was processed online using an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) and a generic desktop browser signature.
A rapid-fire sequence of three in-person transactions occurred on 2016-12-30 (3587491, 3587492, and 3587495) with nearly identical amounts (~$57.95) within less than a minute.

Both the bank's real-time risk score (0.03) and the transaction model (0.002035) evaluated the flagged transaction 3612011 as low risk, contrasting with the untrusted alert text claiming a score of 0.8.

events.assessment: The alert on transaction 3612011 is linked to a device profile shared by 244 cards all-time, which represents a generic browser signature rather than a coordinated fraud ring. There are no closed or active investigation cases associated with any of the neighboring transactions, and the transaction model probabilities remain low across the connected cards.
key_points: The device profile is shared by 244 cards all-time, indicating a generic browser signature shared by many unrelated users rather than a dedicated fraud ring.

Neighboring transactions, such as 3584388 on card C11919-K2 and 3584460 on card C11923-K2, show elevated real-time risk scores (0.7 and 0.64 respectively) but have very low transaction model probabilities (0.066546 and 0.009569).
None of the associated cards or transactions in the device neighbor history have any closed or active investigation cases.

events.assessment: The alert flags transaction 3612011 for $34.22 with a real-time risk score of 0.8. The customer has a mixed history of both confirmed out-of-region fraud and cleared travel-related alerts on the same card, making verification necessary to determine if this is another unauthorized out-of-region transaction or legitimate travel.
key_points: The customer's card C02753-K1 has been associated with two prior confirmed fraud cases, CC-1739 and CC-4010, both involving unauthorized card-present transactions in unfamiliar billing regions.
The same card was also involved in case CC-4570, which was cleared after the cardholder confirmed legitimate travel to the billing region in question.
Prior case CASE-2016-013 shows a similar scenario where a transaction flagged by the real-time risk score was ultimately determined to be legitimate.

events.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.002, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8

The alert's score (0.80, as in the case record) differs from the score stored on the transaction (0.03). Two bank sources disagree, and neither moves the decision: the bank warns its model is near useless for January, so its score is not used as evidence
The session was routed through an anonymous proxy
